apply-canary-fail._why: A canary FAIL is not a record of a measurement that passed. `staging.md` § The three outcomes aborts registration on FAIL, so writing the durable `platform-local.md` on that result would make `audit.md` Step 4b return `PASS (on record)` for a host whose delegation semantics measurably differ from the design's. Identical arguments to apply-canary-record except C2's verdict — the pair isolates the refusal to that one token, and `not` asserts that no part of the file body was emitted on the way out.

apply-canary-record._why: THE PRODUCER FOR A FILE THAT HAD ONLY CONSUMERS. Four documents (`audit.md` Step 4b/6a/7, `verify.md`, `staging.md`, `platform.md`) read `.claude/workforce/platform-local.md` and nothing wrote it; measured 2026-08-06 on this repository, a run recorded `INV-CANARY … PASS` in org-config.md and left no such file. DISPLAY is the default here as everywhere in wf-apply: the exact bytes are printed and nothing is written, which is what `not` asserts. `--measured-on` is pinned so the case is host-independent; the `claude --version` path was exercised by hand on 2026-08-06 and emitted `MEASURED-ON:  Claude Code 2.1.223` unaided. The escaped `\|` matters — canary evidence contains a pipe verbatim, and an unescaped one ends the table cell.

apply-canary-record-execute._why: `--execute` is the consent, same as every other pass in this script. Same tree and same arguments as apply-canary-record; the flag is the only difference and the verb changes from `would write` to `wrote`. `verified on disk:` is asserted because the confirmation RE-READS the file rather than echoing the string that was passed to write() — the defect being closed is a write that was believed and never made, so a report quoting its own input would reproduce it.
want: verified on disk: MEASURED-ON:  Claude Code 2.1.223

apply-deadhook._why: DISPLAY is the default and must change nothing. Three registrations are live, dead, and UNDECIDABLE (a bare `jq` resolved on PATH). Only the two dead ones are named; calling the undecidable one dead would invite deleting a working registration, which is the failure wf-census's DEAD/UNDECIDABLE split exists for. `would apply` rather than `applied` is the whole difference between the two modes.

apply-deadhook-execute._why: --execute is the consent. Same tree as apply-deadhook; the only difference is the flag, and the verdict word changes from `would apply` to `applied`. Paired so a regression that makes display WRITE, or execute merely REPORT, fails one of them.

apply-emptyroot._why: wf-apply's plain (non-record-canary) DISPLAY path on a minimal root. The tree carries exactly one throwaway canary, .claude/agents/wf-canary-a.md, so PASS-STALE-CANARY has one named target; DISPLAY is the default, so the target and the --execute consent gate are printed and nothing is applied. Without a row the fixture tree was on disk and unasserted — a detector with no proof.

apply-stalecanary._why: THREE populations in one tree and only one is residue: a throwaway canary (no measures-fact:), a SHIPPED canary (carries measures-fact:, its job recurs per host and per harness version, never residue), and a real employee. Precision is a property of the three required conditions rather than a sample, and this asserts all three by naming what must NOT appear.

census-deadhook._why: Three registrations: one live, one whose script was deleted, and one `jq` resolved on PATH. The jq row must be UNDECIDABLE, never dead -- calling it dead invites deleting a working registration. --json is asserted separately for per-skill ownership, which is the input set sweep step 5 relocates from.

census-indented-mention._why: In markdown an indented line is a code block, so an indented sacred marker is documentation ABOUT the format and never a span opener. bin/baseline established this and measured 68 naive against 37 anchored -- 46% inflation -- and the other readers never got the ruling. Measured on odyssey-alive 2026-08-05: wf-census reported 118 sacred blocks and two were a template example carrying a literal YYYY-MM-DD, so a directive guard fired on a date format string. The mention is REPORTED, never silently dropped: a number that shrank without explanation is its own defect. Both halves are asserted -- the real block is counted, the indented one is not, and the mention count is printed.

census-order._why: wf-census must name the tree BEFORE it counts anything in it. Commit 26ec383 appended the skills row above the title line, so every report opened with an orphan row above its header — a defect invisible in a diff because both lines are correct in isolation and only their ORDER is wrong. `want` asserts the title line is immediately followed by the skills row; `not` asserts the reverse (skills above a title) is absent, so a reversion fails this case.

changes-current._why: `--from` the INSTALLED version has nothing after it. Written with `${VERSION}` rather than a literal: the case is about the current release, not about 1.31.0, and a pinned number made this fail on every version bump (fixed 2026-09-09 after seven bumps in one afternoon).

checkrun-ambiguous._why: `ambiguous-markup` is the only ALWAYS-blocking row and had no fixture, while being produced by the masker rewritten in four separate rounds. An UNCLOSED FENCE is the canonical trigger; an unclosed HTML wrapper deliberately is not -- with lookahead it is ignored rather than quarantining the file, which is right once nothing executes: masking less risks a reporting miss, never a run.

checkrun-dead._why: A named check whose script is not on disk -- the analogue of dead wiring, and caught by RESOLUTION ALONE with no --run. A dead check reads as protection and enforces nothing.

checkrun-dead-also-in-prose._why: THE MECHANICAL VERDICT MUST WIN. The prose/fence token pass ran first and claimed the path, so a script named BOTH in a sentence and in a declared Check: produced only the non-blocking heuristic row -- exit 0, `0 blocking finding(s)`, which is exactly the 'printed clean' outcome this whole change exists to end. No fixture reached it because every dead-check fixture had a ## Verification containing nothing but the Check: line: fixtures written by the same hand as the extractor. Both shapes here -- prose sentence AND an untagged fence, which the IC template invites a handbook to include.

checkrun-envprefix._why: THE REGRESSION SEGMENT-WALKING INTRODUCED, caught the same hour by running the changed resolver against a real project rather than against its own fixtures. `printf '{...}' | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/home/... bash .claude/hooks/guard.sh` is the ordinary shape of a hook self-test. Walking to the second segment finally reached it -- and its first token is the ENVIRONMENT ASSIGNMENT, which carries a slash in its value, so it read as the path being run and a live hook was reported dead. The pre-fix code scored this silent, not correct: `printf` has no slash, so it stopped at segment one. Fixing the tokenizer without bringing the shell's command-prefix grammar along traded a silence for a false positive on a real tree.

checkrun-extensionless._why: The under-capture hole the SHARED resolver closes. `bash bin/verify` has no extension and no anchor, so the token pass correctly refuses to call it a file reference -- wf-census.resolve_hook_command unwraps the interpreter and answers it. Without the import this case is silently clean, which is the shape of every 'reported clean about something it never examined' defect in this repo.

checkrun-glob._why: `src/**/*.css` is this project's OWN canonical example. EXT_RX matched `.css`, so it resolved as a path and reported a blocking `dead` row -- every handbook copied from the shipped template failed. A glob is not a file. (The `want` clause was vacuous TWICE: `ran` matched 'qua-ran-tined', then `resolved` matched the always-printed summary '0 resolved'. It now keys on the ROW GLYPH, which appears only when a real row is emitted -- verified by deleting the Check: line and watching it fail.)

checkrun-indented-wrapper._why: Branch ORDER alone cannot separate two cases the gate found in successive rounds: with HTML first, an indented <div> with no closer quarantined the file; with indent first, an INDENTED <details> whose body is DEDENTED went live and its illustration was read as a real declaration. Lookahead for the matching closer is what distinguishes them.

checkrun-nested-decorated._why: Two invisibility bugs at once: os.listdir missed .claude/agents/<dept>/, and a byte-exact heading match read `## Verification (mechanical)` as no-section so the check never ran. (The `not` matches the ROW glyph, not the bare word: `no-section` also appears in the summary counts, where a zero is the passing signal.)

checkrun-notpaths._why: REGRESSION GUARD for the two extractor bugs a real tree found on first run. `/text-eval` is a slash command and `agents/interface-claim-auditor/` an unanchored prose fragment; neither is a file and reporting either as dead invites deleting a working check. The first version also stripped the leading dot off `.claude/...`, reporting 0 resolved and 19 dead where all 19 were on disk -- so the resolved row here is load-bearing too.

checkrun-operator._why: FALSE DEAD, the defect a project audit filed against this distribution from another repo on 2026-08-10 and could not fix from its own tree. `shlex.split` is a word splitter with no knowledge of shell operators, so `bash bin/real.sh; echo done` yielded the token `bin/real.sh;` -- semicolon fused on -- which is not a path on any disk. A live script was reported dead, and because a dead check is BLOCKING for a governed handbook the tool exited 1 on a handbook whose check was fine. `bin/real.sh` is present in the fixture tree, so `+ resolved` can only be reached by an operator-aware tokenizer; `not` asserts the false row is gone rather than merely outvoted.

checkrun-operator-dead._why: THE FALSIFICATION HALF of checkrun-operator, and the reason that case cannot pass vacuously. Identical shape, one token changed: `bin/gone.sh` is NOT in the tree. A fix that made the false positive disappear by resolving less -- or by skipping any command carrying a separator -- passes checkrun-operator and fails here. The detail line is asserted verbatim as `bin/gone.sh` with no trailing semicolon, because the pre-fix run reported the same file dead for the wrong reason and a report naming a path that was never on disk under that spelling teaches an author nothing.

checkrun-orphan-negative._why: A Negative with no Check vanished from BOTH passes -- the falsify block returns early on no checks, and the resolver had already stripped the Negative line.

checkrun-placeholder._why: content-writer's actual shape: `... <draft>`, an argument the handbook never binds. The hook EXISTS here, so `resolved` passes and the finding is solely that the command cannot be executed as written -- which is why no one ever ran it.

checkrun-subshell._why: THE SILENT HALF of the same defect, found by writing the pair rather than by any report -- the audit that filed the false-dead row never saw this one. `cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" && bash bin/real.sh` put `cd` in first position: no slash, so UNDECIDABLE, so the real script behind `&&` was never examined and the tool exited 0 having checked nothing. Under-reporting is the direction wf-census.load_ignore is explicitly written against, and it is the direction that hurts. `0 resolved` is asserted absent because that -- not a wrong row -- is what the failure looked like.

claudemd-absent._why: An absent CLAUDE.md is the GOAL STATE (SKILL.md - Directives, 2026-08-05), not a gap to fill. This fixture asserted the opposite until then -- it required the script to CREATE the file containing the generated region, which under the evacuation directive would have one audit writing the file it then deletes, and re-creating it on every later run of an already-evacuated project. Inverted rather than removed: the superseded behaviour is exactly the drift a future edit would reintroduce, because its own comment read well.
want: ABSENT — this is the goal state

claudemd-ensure-region._why: --ensure-region runs at the spawn preflight, BEFORE any handbook exists. It must never classify or remove a user line: this tree carries a line that plain mode reports as DUPLICATED, and ensure-region must not mention it at all.
want: no user line is classified or removed

claudemd-ensure-region-present._why: A stale region from an older run is REPLACED, not doubled. The region regex strips any prior region before the new one is placed, which is what makes the mode idempotent — bin/idempotence asserts the second run writes the same bytes.

claudemd-evacuated._why: Every directive line reached a component — one a handbook, one the org charter — so the ledger is empty and CLAUDE.md may be deleted. DUPLICATED lines are counted as relocated because that is what duplicated MEANS; counting only the USER bucket made a two-rule fixture report one, understating the direction in the file.

claudemd-unevacuated._why: Same tree plus ONE rule that reached no component. Exit 1, the line is named, and the refusal says why: a line that arrived nowhere was not moved, it was lost. Paired with claudemd-evacuated so a regression that always-permits or always-refuses fails one.

companion-drifted._why: THE DEFECT THE WHOLE SCRIPT EXISTS FOR. audit.md Step 4 said 'force-refresh the Core skills every run' in prose with no producer, so it never ran: measured on claude-workforce itself, .claude/skills/org carried 11 dispatch rungs against the shipped 15 across three audits. The marked region here is deliberately behind shipped source, and the two hand-written lines around it are what a refresh must NOT touch.

companion-drifted-execute._why: The same tree with --execute. Only the machine-owned region is replaced; operating-principles has no region and is REPORTED rather than overwritten, because audit-setup.md Step 0.3 state 3 holds that the customization is the requirement and the shipped copy is the newcomer. A run that 'succeeded' by overwriting it would have deleted this project's own principles.

companion-halfmarker._why: One marker without its pair. procedures/org.md step 5: REPORT and SKIP, never auto-repair -- guessing where the missing END belongs is how a partial hand-edit gets overwritten. NO-REGION is counted in unrefreshed and names its precondition, so the run cannot skip it silently and still close clean.

want: `tools:` is a real allowlist, not the display string
one-entry allowlist naming a tool that does not exist

conform-canary-mismatch._why: NEGATIVE. org-config.md records INV-CANARY PASS on harness 2.1.223, but platform-local.md is stamped MEASURED-ON 2.1.100 — a record taken on a different harness cannot answer whether it matches the running one, so Step 4b would return `PASS (on record)` for a measurement made elsewhere. Asserts the DEFECT IS NAMED with both versions, not merely a non-zero exit.
want: canary record: platform-local.md MEASURED-ON matches the recorded harness

conform-canary-recorded._why: POSITIVE half of the mismatch pair. org-config.md records INV-CANARY PASS AND platform-local.md exists with MEASURED-ON 2.1.223 matching the harness org-config records — the reconciliation has its durable record, so wf-conform passes. `not` asserts the canary-record check did not fire a failure against a healthy record. The count moved 2 → 3 when INV-COMPANIONS landed (2026-08-26): this tree has an org-config.md but ZERO governed handbooks, so no audit finished here and INV-COMPANIONS emits its no-population row rather than staying silent — a check that skips must say so, or it is indistinguishable from one that passed.

conform-canary-unavailable._why: POSITIVE half of the unrecorded pair, and the case that proves the check is not a blunt file-exists test. NO platform-local.md exists, yet wf-conform must NOT fail — because the INV-CANARY row records UNAVAILABLE, not PASS, and an unmeasured host owes no record. `not` asserts it did not wrongly flag the absent file.

conform-canary-unrecorded._why: NEGATIVE, and this project's signature failure made testable: org-config.md records INV-CANARY PASS while platform-local.md is ABSENT — the measurement was taken and never written down, exactly the state a real audit left on 2026-08-06. Asserts the DEFECT IS NAMED, not merely a non-zero exit.
want: canary record: INV-CANARY records PASS and platform-local.md exists

conform-companions-missing._why: NEGATIVE half of the INV-COMPANIONS pair (invariants.md row 23). An audit finished in this tree — org-config.md is present AND one governed handbook is staffed — and five of the six core companions were materialized while `.claude/skills/org/SKILL.md` was not. MEASURED: an audit ran TWICE on a fresh project and never created /org, reporting clean both times, because audit-setup.md Step 0.3 said 'install the shipped version' and the distribution ships NO companion skill directory, so a literal run reasoned 'ships none → install none'. Nothing failed the skip. Asserts the DEFECT IS NAMED — the missing path, and /org called out as the hard failure because it is GENERATED by `org index` and no installer will ever fetch it — not merely a non-zero exit. The five present companions are what make this a real negative: a check that merely tested 'any skill exists' would pass here. COUNT FORM (2026-09-02): the summary assertion is `1 governed` + the RELATIVE `checks · 1 failed`, not the absolute `20 checks · 1 failed` it carried before. The absolute pin was measuring the whole org-wide check total from a fixture that owns ONE invariant, so every unrelated row added anywhere reddened it — and because advisory rows count into that total, v1.6.0's REQUEST-verbatim and workforce-version rows plus v1.7.0's Sources row moved it 20 → 24 with nothing about companions having changed. Re-measured value at the time of the change: 24. Detection is not weakened: this half names the row text `✗ INV-COMPANIONS: ...` and demands exit 1, so a deleted or silenced check fails HERE and says which one — strictly louder than a total sliding 20 → 19, which names nothing. `1 governed` is the replacement vacuity guard and the one the absolute count was really standing in for: if discovery broke, 0 governed would yield 0 checks and 0 failed, and the POSITIVE twin would pass quietly.
want: ✗ INV-COMPANIONS: every core companion skill exists after an audit

conform-companions-present._why: POSITIVE half of the INV-COMPANIONS pair. The SAME audited tree as conform-companions-missing — org-config.md, one governed handbook — with all six core companions on disk at .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. It differs from its negative twin by EXACTLY ONE FILE, so a regression that stops detecting the absence fails the negative and a regression that fires against a complete set fails this one; neither case alone distinguishes those. The pair differs only in the failed count: `checks · 0 failed` here against `checks · 1 failed` in the negative, over the same tree. SUPERSEDED (2026-09-02): this used to pin the absolute `20 checks` on both halves, on the reasoning that a check which stopped running would drop the total and fail here rather than passing quietly. The negative twin does that job better — it wants the literal `✗ INV-COMPANIONS: ...` row and exit 1, so a check that stops running fails there BY NAME — while the absolute total coupled this fixture to every check and advisory in the script (advisory rows count into `N checks`) and went stale twice without companions changing, 20 → 24. What actually guarded against a vacuous pass here was never the 20; it was that SOMETHING ran, so that is now asserted directly as `1 governed`: if discovery broke, 0 governed → 0 checks → 0 failed would satisfy a bare `0 failed` and this half would pass on an unsurveyed tree. wf-conform prints only failing and advisory rows, so a PASSING row's own text is unobservable on stdout and this half cannot assert it — the same limit conform-canary-recorded works within, and it is stated rather than papered over. `not` carries the bare string INV-COMPANIONS: on a healthy tree the invariant must not appear in the report at all.

conform-ignored-corpus._why: TWO CHECKERS, ONE TREE, TWO DENOMINATORS -- the row a project audit filed alongside checkrun-operator, and the one with teeth: it was the sole reason wf-conform exited 1, which holds INV-VERIFY at NOT UPHELD and aborts any future sweep. `.censusignore` had three readers and one producer; wf-census and wf-apply honoured the declaration and wf-conform's sacred-block walk pruned a directory literally named `fixtures` and read nothing else. The fixture declares `.claude/skills/thing/testdata/` -- deliberately NOT named `fixtures`, so only a reader of the declaration can exclude it -- and puts an unstamped sacred block inside. sidecar-uncovered is the falsification half and stays red: an UNDECLARED unstamped block must still fail, or this fix is just a disabled check.

conform-invokes-spawner._why: TRUE POSITIVE GUARD for the routing exemption added 2026-08-05. A tier-3 IC that plainly invokes a spawning skill, with no escalation vocabulary anywhere, MUST still fail. The exemption was added because 22 of 22 findings on a real org were re-homed steps; this is the case that proves the exemption narrowed the check rather than disabled it.
want: invokes only skills that spawn nothing (/spawnyskill)

conform-mcp-slug-bare._why: THE NEGATIVE FOR THE THREE EXCLUSIONS ABOVE. A bare `widget-mcp` that is not a skill, not the project's name and not inside a path is still a dependency and still fails. Without this row the exclusions could be widened to nothing and every fixture would stay green — a check discounted into silence is the failure `verify.md` § BLOCKING names.
want: every MCP server its body uses is named in tools:

conform-mcp-slug-in-path._why: A slug with a `/` on either side is a directory, not an invocation — the same mention-is-not-use rule the `/skill` branch already applies to path fragments.

conform-mcp-slug-is-skill._why: A bare `<name>-mcp` that resolves to `.claude/skills/<name>-mcp/SKILL.md` is a SKILL, reached through `Skill()`, and a skill grants nothing and needs nothing in `tools:`. MEASURED 2026-09-05 on playwright-mcp: `build-mcp` is a skill and it produced a BLOCKING failure in 4 of 6 handbooks. The `mcp__` invocation form is untouched, so this exclusion cannot hide a dependency an employee actually calls.

want: every MCP server its body uses is named in tools:

conform-no-negative._why: A governed handbook with a Check: and NO Negative:. The advisory row must fire and the exit code must stay 0 -- the contract post-dates every handbook under it, and failing them all reproduces the 9-false-failures run that taught this script 'a check that always fails stops being read'. The bin/check assertion can only see that the channel EXISTS; only this can see that it does not block. `1 advisory` is an EXACT total and it is load-bearing: the fixture handbook is deliberately clean of every OTHER advisory, so the count means the no-negative row and nothing else, and a row that fired unconditionally on any handbook would push it to 2 and fail here. MEASURED 2026-09-02: `1 governed · 18 checks · 0 failed · 1 advisory`. CONTRACT FOR WHOEVER ADDS THE NEXT ADVISORY: silence it on THIS handbook (give it the section it asks for), do not re-pin the count -- re-pinning to 2 destroys the discrimination this case exists for. That is how it went stale: v1.6.0 added the REQUEST-verbatim and workforce-version rows and v1.7.0 added the Sources row, all three fired here, the total read 4, and nobody re-measured. Fixed by giving the handbook a `## Sources` reading `(none)` (correct measured value for a pure reviewer role), a workforce-version stamp, and a REQUEST (verbatim) Reporting contract -- NOT by moving the pin. The deliberate defect, the absent `Negative:` line, is untouched. The handbook is stamped `workforce-version: 99.0.0` rather than a real release: each of these fixtures isolates ONE advisory, and a stamp older than the install would add the superseded-doctrine row to every count here and break them all on every version bump. 99.0.0 is never older than the install, so the row stays silent and the case keeps testing its own subject. Restamped 2026-09-05 when that row shipped. Advisory count raised by one on 2026-09-07: wf-conform gained the say-the-state row (every finding reports its outcome; no work handed up the chain you could do; no finding downgraded afterwards), and these fixture handbooks predate the clause, so each picks up exactly one more advisory. The number is asserted rather than the row list because the count is what proves the row fired on the right population.

conform-over-ceiling._why: TWO defects in one row, both measured. (1) CHANNEL: delegation-budget.md has always said over the ceiling is never a refusal, but the row was wired to the blocking channel, so 14 of them set a non-zero exit on odyssey-alive (2026-08-05) and INV-VERIFY read that exit as the org failing to verify. The advisory marker plus exit 0 plus no '✗ ' anywhere is what pins it to res.advise(). (2) WORDING: the message read 'a structural finding proposing a split', and 'proposing' is a hand-back — it was being cashed out as an optional 'want me to split these?' offer and an AskUserQuestion picker offering 'leave as-is' or 'trim', which the no-standing-queue directive (2026-08-10) forbids and which risks dropping the user's verbiage (directive one is retention). The run PERFORMS the split by relocation this run, so 'proposing' must NOT appear and the performed/relocated wording must. Paired with conform-under-ceiling: drop the advisory and this half fails; fire it unconditionally and that half fails. (3) THE NUMBER: this row read 150 until 2026-09-07, four days after delegation-budget.md measured the floor at 172 and retired 150 outright — the fixture was asserting a number its own doctrine had dropped. bin/check now compares wf-conform's constant against the sentence in delegation-budget.md that retires 150, so the two cannot drift again; the fixture handbook is 230 lines so it clears the higher ceiling and the case still fires.
want: the split is PERFORMED this run
Never trimmed, never condensed, never handed back as a question

conform-removal-staged._why: The same tree with Step 6-S having run: T7s writes SKILL.md.orig and tree/, T7c writes the mark, and T2's extraction record exists for the one sacred span the target holds. MUST pass. Paired with conform-removal-unstaged (the mark is missing) and conform-removal-unextracted (the extraction is missing) so each half of Step 6-S has a fixture that fails without it. `tree/` is asserted because the sweep unlinks the WHOLE directory — references/, scripts/, hooks/, datasets — and SKILL.md.orig is an undo for the least of that.

conform-removal-unextracted._why: T2 IS THE ONE GATE BETWEEN A DIRECTORY DELETION AND THE USER'S OWN WORDS, and it was specified without being computable: INV-DIRECTIVES counts N of N TREE-WIDE while T2 for a removal target asks a DIRECTORY-scoped question, and wf-census published only the aggregate. The only way to answer it was a hand grep — which on 2026-08-06 reported 37 sacred spans in skill-builder against the true 6, by matching indented examples and markers quoted mid-line inside the file that DOCUMENTS the marker format. Staged, marked, undo on disk, and one span unextracted: the target must be named with its file:line, not with the difference between two totals.

conform-removal-unstaged._why: THE REMOVAL SET HAD A READER AND NO WRITER. `sweep.md` derives it from the journal; `conversion-taxonomy.md` decided the removals and never wrote a journal row; `T7c` was inserted as the mark 2026-08-04 with no row shape defined for it. Measured on odyssey-alive over three audits: `skill-builder` dispositioned SUPERSEDED GENERATOR, on disk throughout, zero rows naming it, 32 T7 rows and zero T7c rows — every run printed an empty removal set and every run was right about the journal. The finding must name the target and the step it is missing, never print a balanced-looking zero.
want: oldgen was dispositioned for removal and staged

conform-routed-escalation._why: The same handbook with the step re-homed exactly as wf-conform's own message recommends. MUST pass. Deliberately built in the hard real-world shape measured on odyssey-alive: the skill is named on one line, the `ESCALATE:` marker sits two lines below carrying only a `<skill>` placeholder, and the sentence that proves the re-homing is inside the same numbered step. A line-local scope, or one that reads the prohibition-filtered text, reports this file.

conform-section-mention._why: REGRESSION GUARD. `## Verification` is MENTIONED in prose at line 2 of ## Procedure before the real heading, so a substring split hands every reader the tail of ## Procedure and the real section is never examined. The fixture's directory name IS the project name, which is what the check reads. MEASURED 2026-09-05: `playwright-mcp` named itself in 5 of 6 handbooks and every mention was a blocking failure.

Sources says WHERE the truth is + HOW to reach it; the Procedure EXERCISES that reach.' Asserts THE DEFECT IS NAMED -- the skill by name, in both the row and its detail -- not merely that some advisory fired, because a row naming no skill leaves the reader to guess which of several channels is dead. Advisory and exit 0 for the same post-dating reason as the presence row. The handbook is stamped `workforce-version: 99.0.0` rather than a real release: each of these fixtures isolates ONE advisory, and a stamp older than the install would add the superseded-doctrine row to every count here and break them all on every version bump. 99.0.0 is never older than the install, so the row stays silent and the case keeps testing its own subject. This tree already carries the user's own Stop hook and a wf-plain-guard registered on PreToolUse/Edit -- a matcher the record does not name. Unwiring must take exactly the two recorded rows and leave both of those, because the whole contract of a mechanism the installer wires without being asked is that its reversal is conservative. Verified by hand on 2026-09-07 and that was ONE OBSERVATION; this file's own harness says a fixture that works once is not a regression test.

seed-dryrun._why: Default (no --execute) is a dry run: it reports the plan and writes NOTHING. `after` asserts the target file gained no region — consent-to-write is --execute, and a dry run that mutates the tree would break the display/execute contract every other writer script honours.

seed-fresh._why: A catalog with an anchor but no WF-ADDITIONS region is the code-evaluator gap that prompted wf-seed. --execute must append the slot VERBATIM as one machine-owned region in a file the evaluator reads and record additions-seeded in the anchor. `after` proves the write, not just the report: a script that says 'region written' while writing nothing is the failure this harness exists to catch.

seed-no-target._why: THE FALSIFYING HALF of the two rows above. Candidate resolution widened where wf-seed looks; this pins that it did not widen what it will WRITE INTO. No candidate exists at either location here — only an unrelated catalog file — so the run must ERROR, exit 3, and NAME every path it tried, never fall back to the first file it happens to see and never invent one. Without this case, a resolver degraded to 'write into any catalog file' would pass seed-refs-subdir and seed-retargeted-text unchanged.
want: region target not found: tried mistake-taxonomy.md, references/mistake-taxonomy.md

seed-refs-subdir._why: LAYOUT, measured on odyssey-alive 2026-08-25: a customized code-evaluator keeps its catalog files under references/, not at the skill root. wf-seed resolved the target at the root only, so it reported `region target mistake-taxonomy.md absent` against a tree that plainly had one and refused to seed the catalog it was written to seed. The target must resolve at root THEN references/, and the anchor must record the path actually written (region-file=references/mistake-taxonomy.md) — a bare name there would send the next run looking at the root again and open a second region. `after` proves both halves: the region landed in the references/ file, and the anchor names that file.

seed-retargeted-text._why: NAMING, the second half of the same 2026-08-25 measurement: text-eval's main catalog is `references/ai-patterns.md` and no `text-tells.md` exists anywhere in the install, yet wf-seed hardcoded `text-tells.md` as the target and errored. `text-tells.md` is workforce's own SLOT filename and stays; only the TARGET is candidate-resolved, first existing wins, so the same slot reaches a retargeted catalog. A second catalog file (colon-detection.md) is present so a resolver that simply took whatever file it found would still be wrong here.

seed-unappendable._why: The ONE blocker: a target file immutable end to end (its origin:user|immutable span runs to EOF) leaves no position to open a region without writing inside it. wf-seed must HOLD, name the file and the spans, write nothing, and STILL exit 0 — a skipped append on a genuinely unappendable catalog is correct behaviour, not a failed pass (evaluators.md § When the catalog cannot be appended).

want: every sacred block on disk is stamped

skill-match-emptyroot._why: `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` is UNSET in the Bash tool, so a shipped `--root "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}"` block expands to `--root ""`, and `os.path.abspath("")` is the CWD — a real directory, which an is-it-a-directory guard passes. A matcher that accepted it would report the skills of whatever tree the caller happened to be standing in, under the name of a role. The guard runs BEFORE stdin is read, so `not` asserts that no part of the named tree and no tier line reached the output: the tool refused the argument instead of surveying a tree nobody named.
want: ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is unset outside a hook; pass an explicit path.

skill-match-nomatch._why: THE NEGATIVE HALF: a role no installed skill serves. An empty answer is an answer — the hire learns the host has nothing for this role — so this must exit 0 with `[]` rather than fail, and `not` forbids a single `"skill":` key, which is the only way to assert the array is EMPTY rather than merely short. The tree has no `home/.claude` at all, so the same case covers the three fail-safes that would otherwise need a crash to discover: an absent personal skills directory, an absent plugins directory, and a `--config-dir` naming neither. The counts line still prints, including its zeroes.
want: role payroll-clerk — 1 skill(s) read, 0 quarantined, 0 unresolved source(s), 0 matched

skill-match-ranked._why: THE RANKED OUTPUT, PINNED IN ORDER, not merely a list containing the right names. A website build hired the right titles while four installed design skills (`frontend-design`, `design`, `dataviz`, `artifact-design`) were never matched to the role, so the handbooks named none of them; this is the producer for that inventory. The three `want` fragments that span an element boundary are what fix RANK: each runs from one entry's `scope` through the next entry's `skill`, which is the longest contiguous run of the array that contains no absolute path, and paths vary because every case runs against a copy at a temp path. Measured on this tree: frontend-design scores 10 (two name hits at 3, four description hits at 1), artifact-design 5, dataviz 3. The tree also carries one skills-container directory with no SKILL.md, one SKILL.md outside any `skills/` container, and one unparseable SKILL.md — all three are asserted as REPORTED, per discovery.md's rule that an unrecognised source is a finding and never a silent skip, and the counts line proves the quarantined one still adds up. `not` holds the HEURISTIC tier restriction: the verdict may cite overlap and may never recommend a merge or a fix.
want: /.claude/skills/notes-only — directory in a skills container with no SKILL.md
/.claude/skills/broken-skill/SKILL.md — no frontmatter name/description, no heading, no first line
4 skill(s) read, 1 quarantined, 2 unresolved source(s), 3 matched

skill-match-stdin._why: THE SECOND INPUT FORM, which has no flags to typo and therefore no argparse error to warn on. A JSON object on stdin must produce the same ranked array as the flag form, and `config_dir` inside that object must be honoured — without it the run would scan the operator's real `~/.claude` and the pinned output would differ per host. The boundary fragment pins rank across the project/personal split, proving the two sources are ranked against each other rather than concatenated in scan order. `not` forbids the two caller errors, because a payload silently ignored would present as an ordinary no-match.
want: role frontend-design — 2 skill(s) read, 0 quarantined, 0 unresolved source(s), 2 matched

stamp-absent-line._why: THE CASE A PLACEHOLDER-ONLY PRODUCER WOULD MISS. `engineering-lead.md` on playwright-mcp carried no `contract-stamp` line at all — the template ships one and the authoring path does not reliably emit it, so 1 handbook in 6 had nothing to replace. A producer that only substituted the placeholder would have reported a clean run over it.

stamp-adopted._why: An ADOPTED agent was censused into the chart with zero bytes changed (conversion-taxonomy.md ADOPT). It carries no ORG-RECORD, and stamping one would write workforce's own field into a file workforce does not own. Skipped BY NAME, never silently — `adopted 1` and `stamped 0` are different claims from a run that saw nothing.

stamp-drift._why: THE NEGATIVE. A real digest that no longer matches the sections is MISMATCH: reported, exit 1, and NEVER rewritten. checksums.md § On mismatch — a legitimate amendment and an unauthorized edit are indistinguishable from the hash, so re-stamping erases the only evidence that something changed. `not` asserts the file is not silently repaired by holding the stale digest in the output; the --execute half of the same guarantee is stamp-drift-execute.

stamp-drift-execute._why: `--execute` alone must not touch a MISMATCH — the refusal is the behaviour, not the display mode. Same tree as stamp-drift with the write flag on: still exit 1, still no write, and `after` proves the stale digest is still on disk. Without this row the refusal lives only in display mode and a regression that repaired on --execute would pass every other case.

stamp-execute._why: The write path, asserted on the ARTIFACT and not only on stdout — script-conformance's `after` exists because a script that writes the wrong thing while reporting fine is invisible to want/not. The placeholder must be GONE and a real 64-hex digest present, because a producer that appends a second stamp line beside the first leaves two contract-stamps and every reader takes whichever it finds first.

stamp-placeholder._why: DISPLAY IS THE DEFAULT and it writes nothing. The shipped template placeholder `(set at registration)` is what five of six real handbooks carried; it is not a digest, so it classifies UNSTAMPED rather than MISMATCH — writing a first stamp over it erases no prior claim and is not the repair checksums.md forbids. `after` proves the display run left the file alone.

stampdir-drift._why: THE NEGATIVE, and the one that matters. A row whose digest no longer matches means the user's own words may have been reworded, and checksums.md § On mismatch forbids repairing it: an authorized amendment and an edit nobody approved are indistinguishable from the hash, so rewriting erases the only evidence that something changed. Exit 1, both digests printed, and `not` asserts nothing was written.

stampdir-drift-execute._why: The refusal is BEHAVIOUR, not a display mode. Same tree as stampdir-drift with the write flag on: still exit 1, still no write, and `after` proves the stale digest is untouched on disk. Without this row the refusal would live only in the reporting path, and a regression that repaired on plain --execute would pass every other case here.

stampdir-ignored._why: Scope is DECLARED, never inferred. A vendored skill excluded by .censusignore carries a real sacred block, and stamping it would freeze someone else's text as this project's directive — the same reason wf-census refuses to count a fixture corpus as user directives. One block in scope, not two, and `not` names the excluded path so a regression that widened the walk fails here rather than passing with a larger number.

stampdir-malformed._why: Readers are liberal but never silent (checksums.md rule 1). A data line the canonical row regex cannot parse is a coverage gap, and the inherited incident this subsystem exists for is exactly a sidecar whose unreadable rows were skipped so the hook reported clean. The line is REPORTED with its text and counted, and a later rewrite drops it in favour of rows that parse.

stampdir-orphan._why: A row naming a block that no longer exists can never be re-hashed, so it reports coverage of nothing — the shape checksums.md calls a sidecar reporting clean about blocks it never examined. It is named in display mode and DROPPED on write, and `after` proves the drop happened while the live row survived. Dropping is safe here and only here: there is no content left to protect.

stampdir-restamp._why: The authorized-amendment path, and the only gesture that may overwrite a DRIFT row. Same tree again with --restamp added, so the pair isolates the write to that one token exactly as apply-canary-fail isolates a refusal to one verdict. `after` proves the stale digest is GONE and the recomputed one is in its place.

stampdir-twoblocks._why: The row index is 1-based and PER FILE, matching how wf-conform reads a row back as `found[i - 1]`. A file holding two sacred blocks must produce :directive:1 and :directive:2 rather than one row for the file — a generator that collapsed them would leave the second block unprotected while the count read as covered.

stampdir-unprotected._why: A sacred block with NO row is UNPROTECTED, and it is not an error — it is the first-run state. Display mode names the block and writes nothing, which `not` asserts. Exit 0 because nothing drifted: an absent row is a coverage gap the next --execute closes, and failing here would leave a fresh install unable to bootstrap its own sidecar.

stampdir-unprotected-execute._why: The write path, asserted on the ARTIFACT. A producer that reports a row it did not write is the exact failure this sidecar subsystem exists for — checksums.md opens by citing a generator whose own parser could not read its rows. `after` proves the canonical grammar `<sha>  <path>:directive:<N>` is on disk with a real digest, and the read-back line proves the script re-parsed what it wrote before counting it.

ledger-badstdin-is-silent._why: A hook that wedges a session over its own bookkeeping is worse than the defect it watches. Unparseable input exits 0 and says nothing.

ledger-counts-bash-as-read._why: MEASURED regression. The first version classified Bash by substring and scored `grep -rn foo . 2>/dev/null` and `python3 bin/check 2>&1 | grep passed` as WRITES, because `>` was on the write list — under-counting exactly the reads this hook exists to surface. There is no classifier now; Bash counts as a read without the command being inspected.

ledger-one-source-read-thrice._why: The failure this hook was built for: one document read three times is ONE piece of evidence, not three. Distinct count is the signal; the raw count is not.

ledger-scopes-to-current-turn._why: Reads belonging to an EARLIER turn must not be credited to this one. A ledger that spans the session grows monotonically and stops meaning anything — the dormancy shape enforcement.md refuses.

ledger-zero-reads._why: A turn that asserts and looked at nothing. NOT an error and never described as one — answering from context in hand is directive two's explicit instruction. The count is reported so a reader need not guess which turns those were.

ledger-names-bare-jargon._why: MEASURED over 4,447 real Opus 5 replies: 7.0% carried this distribution's own coined vocabulary bare in prose written for a human - the LARGEST of the four defect classes measured that day, against 2.9% for unsourced causal claims and 0.3% for caving openers. Unlike the substring guard retired at 7.0% false positives (changes/1.30.1.md), these words have no ordinary meaning to match, so a fire means the term is genuinely there. It reports and names the term; it never blocks.

ledger-masks-code-spans._why: The false-positive class, removed by measurement rather than by caution. Unmatched, `dormant` inside a probe FILENAME and `fan-out` inside a table cell of identifiers both fired - masking code spans dropped the rate from 7.0% to 5.2% and took that whole class with it. A backticked term NAMES an artifact; a bare one asks the reader to decode it.

ledger-silent-on-plain-prose._why: A reply that says what it did in words the reader already knows draws no PLAIN line. The guard that died taught that a checker firing on good output teaches a reader to stop reading the checker.
